newsitem.title: USA: Sears says February softlines sales strong.
newsitem.headline: Sears says February softlines sales strong.

text.p: Sears Roebuck and Co said February sales of hardline products were hurt by a drop in seasonal products, while softlines sales were strong.
"Sears softlines sales remained strong in February," said chairman and chief executive Arthur Martinez.
"Our full-line stores continued to generate double-digit increases in women's ready to wear, children's apparel, shoes, cosmetics and fine jewelry," he said.

Off-the-mall formats posted solid comparable store gains. "We are pleased by the growing contribution from our new store program, which has resulted in total revenues growing significantly more than comparable store sales," he said.
Total domestic store revenues for the four weeks ending March 1 were $1.82 billion, 5.7 percent above $1.72 billion for the four weeks ending March 2, 1996, Sears reported.
Comparable domestic store revenues increased 1.6 percent, versus a 5.1 percent increase in the same period a year ago.
For the four weeks ending March 1, Sears reported total revenues of $2.58 billion, 6.9 percent above the $2.42 billion in the prior-year period.
